title: Heuristic evaluation + customer intercept insights (July 2026)
summary: Combined heuristic review and lightweight intercept usability study run against the beta console. Goal: surface high-impact UI friction that blocks common ops (model switch, rollout config, cost preview) and propose quick remediation for the July sprint.
objectives: Validate model selection workflow clarity for new users and platform admins
Identify points of confusion during rollout/canary config (traffic %, fallback policy)
Gather verbatim customer language to inform copy and microcopy changes
Produce prioritized, implementable backlog items (quick wins + experiments)
participants: Intercept participants: 18 beta users (mix of ML engineers, infra platform engineers, and a couple PMs) - sessions unmoderated, ~5-12 minutes each
Heuristic reviewers: 5 (UX, Product, Sr. PM, Eng Lead, SRE)
method: Two parallel streams run June 30 - July 6: 1) Heuristic evaluation across key flows (model selection, rollout creation, route-level cost preview) using Nielsen heuristics + Redwood-specific checklist; 2) Unmoderated intercept test embedded in beta console (task-based prompts, optional screen recording, short survey at end). Analysis combined both data sources and prioritized by severity * frequency * customer value.
tasks: T1: Create a new rollout that sends 20% traffic to new model variant; set automatic fallback after 5% error rate
T2: Preview and interpret cost delta between quantized and full-precision model options for a 10k token/day workload
T3: Pin a model version to a route and later unpin it
T4: Find where to enable KV cache and estimate latency impact
T5: Identify where audit/logging for private deployments is exposed
raw_observations: (P4) 'Where do I pick the kernel? I thought that happened automatically' - confusion about advanced runtime toggles
(P9) Spent ~90s looking for fallback policy after creating rollout; assumed it was part of rollout form but it's in a separate tab
(P12) 'Cost preview is vague — what does cost per request mean vs per-token?'
Heuristic: model selector overloaded with many dropdowns; inconsistency in how variants are named (v1 vs model-2026-06)
Heuristic: lack of progressive disclosure for advanced settings causes cognitive load on first-run users
(Recording sample) Several participants clicked the help icon, then left the page to search docs — documentation not surfaced inline
top_findings: 1) Model selection ambiguity (Severity: High): Dropdown mixes model families, quantization profiles, and version tags without clear affordances. Impact: mistakes when pinning causing unexpected cost/regression. Frequency: 13/18. Recommendation: split into two-step selector (family -> variant) and surface a small badge for quantization and latency profile.

2) Rollout/fallback discoverability (Severity: High): Fallback policy is not surfaced in the rollout creation flow; users think it's automatic. Impact: potential outages when new variant behaves badly. Frequency: 10/18. Recommendation: add fallback block in rollout form with default 'use stable variant' and inline explanation.

3) Cost preview language mismatch (Severity: Medium): 'Cost per request' vs 'per-token' not explained; users misinterpret cost estimates. Impact: purchasing decisions and overcommit. Frequency: 9/18. Recommendation: reword to 'Estimated cost per 1,000 tokens' and show example calculation for chosen input size.

4) Advanced runtime controls exposure (Severity: Medium): Kernel/quantization toggles are shown by default in some routes. Impact: non-expert users change settings and get worse performance. Recommendation: collapse advanced controls behind 'Advanced settings' with descriptions and 'recommended' presets.

5) Help and docs flow (Severity: Low): Help icon opens modal with dense docs; users leave console to read full pages. Recommendation: create 2–3 inline tooltips and a contextual 'Learn more' drawer linking to expanded docs and short video.
6) Naming & versioning UX (Severity: Low): Variant names rely on build timestamps; users prefer human-friendly aliases. Recommendation: add user-editable alias field with optional autogenerated name
quick_wins: Add small helper text under 'Model' dropdown: 'Choose family → then pick a variant. Quantized variants have (Q) badge.' — estimated 1 sprint, owner: Marco
Move fallback policy into the rollout creation form as a required small panel with a smart default — 1 sprint, owner: Evelyn, JIRA: CON-4821
Change cost preview header copy to 'Estimated cost per 1k tokens' + add inline example calculator — 1 sprint, owner: Tomás
Collapse 'Kernel/Quantization' section under an 'Advanced' expander and default to recommended profile — quick CSS + copy change (0.5 sprint)
Add one-line contextual tooltip for 'KV cache' with link to docs — small frontend change

CON-4830: Model selector two-step redesign + (Q) badge (Priority: P0, Estimate: 8, Owner: Marco)
CON-4835: Cost preview rewrite + micro-calculator (Priority: P1, Estimate: 3, Owner: Tomás)

wireframe-notes: Updated Figma file contains a 2-step model selector (family window then variants list with badges), an expanded rollout form with fallback, and a sticky cost preview summary in the bottom-right. Designer notes: consider micro-animations for variant badges to show latency/cost tradeoff. See linked Figma file for frames and component spec.
open_questions: Should fallback default be 'stable variant' or 'region fallback' for multi-region customers? (ops input needed)
Do we expose quantization labels as warnings or as recommended presets? (PM + Research decision)
How to measure success for rollout discoverability change? Suggest metrics: % of rollouts created with fallback set, incidents caused by rollouts, time-to-complete rollout task
